question: What will the first reported earnings per share after September 2026 be for the following companies? (Meta)

calls.reasoning: Meta guided (Aug 2026) to accrue ~$10B legal expense in Q3 2026 for the state-AG youth-harm settlement, excluded from the July expense outlook. Ex-charge GAAP EPS models to ~$6.5-6.8 (rev ~$63.3-64B, opex ~$44B, tax 15-17%, 2.565B diluted shares), matching the $6.60-6.76 consensus. The charge is ~$3.9/share pre-tax, so ~$3.3-3.9 after tax depending on deductibility, giving GAAP EPS of ~$2.6-3.6. The true below-range probability is ~95%+, but declared escape mass is capped at 0.5; percentiles cover the unlikely in-range case (charge deferred or a large tax benefit like Q1's $8B), clustered near the lower bound. The $5.94 consensus likely mixes charge-inclusive and charge-exclusive estimates. No Polymarket, Kalshi, Manifold or bookmaker market found.

- Meta 8-K/statements (late Aug 2026): expects to accrue ~$10B legal expense in Q3 2026 for the settlement with 51 state AGs (about $12.19B over 10 years, up to ~$16.7-17.1B contingent on other platforms). Sources: CNBC 2026-09-02, gate.com, techi.com Oct 2026.
- techi.com (Oct 2026): the $10B charge was 'not contemplated' in the July FY2026 expense range of $165-169B. Q3 revenue guide $61-64B.
- Q2 2026 8-K exhibit 99.1: revenue $60.80B, costs $42.03B (incl. $2.4B legal + $1.2B severance), op income $18.78B, tax rate 16%, net income $15.85B, diluted shares 2,566M, diluted EPS $6.18 (missed ~$7.2 consensus).
- Q1 2026 (CNBC 2026-04-29): costs $33.44B, op income $22.87B, GAAP EPS $10.44 including an $8.03B tax benefit (+$3.13/share).
- H1 2026 costs $75.47B, so H2 ex-charge implies $89.5-93.5B; Q3 ex-charge roughly $43-45B.
- Consensus revenue ~$63.3B (TradingView). EPS consensus quoted variously as $6.60, $6.66, $6.76 (likely ex-charge) and $5.94 (Zacks/CNBC; possibly a mix).
- Arithmetic: ~$10B pre-tax / 2.565B shares = $3.90/share; after-tax $3.28 if deductible at 16%, $3.90 if not deductible (IRC 162(f) restricts deductibility of payments to governments except restitution/remediation). Deductibility not disclosed (searched, absent).
- Precedent: Q3 2025 GAAP EPS $1.05 after a one-time $15.9B tax charge vs ~$7 underlying.
- Status quo: the charge is booked as guided and GAAP EPS reflects it. Not found: any statement that the charge timing changed, or any Q3 tax benefit.
- Markets: none found on Polymarket or Manifold (harness search); none on Kalshi.

calls.reconciliation: All three runs agreed on the facts: $10B Q3 accrual, ex-charge EPS ~6.6-6.8, GAAP ~2.8-4.5, p_below_lower capped at 0.5. The only dispute was how to shape the in-range percentiles, a judgment call. One check confirmed the charge is still expected in Q3 and that BofA cut its EPS estimate from $7.08 to $3.79, an implied $3.29 hit consistent with a deductible charge at ~16% tax. I found no evidence of deferral. On the in-range shape I sit between Run 1 (tightest) and Run 3: partial-charge outcomes cluster near the bound, full deferral sits near 6.6-7.1.
